title: Behold, on Zion's Heavenly Shore
description: Behold, on Zion's Heavenly Shore in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Hosea Ballou wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 561 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Heavenly Zion”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold, on Zi-on's heav-enly shore, A pure and count-less band, Whose con-flicts and whose toils are o'er, In glo-rious or-der stand.

lines: Whose conflicts and whose toils are o'er,
From earth's remotest bounds they came,
And, through the victories of the Lamb,
Hunger and thirst they know no more,
The Lamb shall feed them from his store,
God all their tears shall wipe away,
While in his temple they shall stay,
And God with them shall dwell.

licence: Public domain: Hosea Ballou died in 1852.
credits: Words by Hosea Ballou (1771–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
